name: Question 1
problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=7\,i+2\,j$ across the circle $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=36.$
worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

The closed curve $C$ is a circle centered at the origin with the radius $6.$ It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

$$
r(t)=6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=6\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =7, \\ Q(x,y) & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=6\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(7)\cdot (6\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(2)\cdot (-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }42\operatorname{cos}⁡t+12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(42\operatorname{sin}⁡t-12\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =(0-12)-(0-12) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate the flux of the vector field F(x,y)=7i+2j across the circle C with equation x2+y2=36.

a
54
b
12
c
24
d
0
e
30
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F=Pi+Qj is a vector field and C is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of F across C is given by ∮CF⋅nds=∮CPdy−Qdx, where n denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to C.

The closed curve C is a circle centered at the origin with the radius 6. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

r(t)=6cos⁡ti+6sin⁡tj,0≤t≤2π.

Along the curve C, we have x=6cos⁡t,y=6sin⁡t.

Therefore,

P(x,y)=7,Q(x,y)=2.

Computing the derivatives of x(t) and y(t) along the curve, we get

dxdt=ddt(6cos⁡t)=−6sin⁡t,dydt=ddt(6sin⁡t)=6cos⁡t.

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

∮CF⋅nds=∮CPdy−Qdx=∫02π(P⋅dydt−Q⋅dxdt)dt=∫02π(7)⋅(6cos⁡t)−(2)⋅(−6sin⁡t)dt=∫02π42cos⁡t+12sin⁡tdt=(42sin⁡t−12cos⁡t)|02π=(0−12)−(0−12)=0
